title: "Debug your configuration - Claude Code Docs"
heading: ​ Check MCP servers
text:
## ​ Check MCP servers
- Project-scoped servers in .mcp.json require a one-time approval. If the prompt was dismissed, the server stays disabled until you approve it from /mcp .
- A server that fails to start shows as failed in /mcp . Relative file paths in command or args are a frequent cause, since they resolve against the directory you launched Claude Code from rather than the location of .mcp.json .
- A server that shows as connected but lists zero tools has started successfully but isn’t returning a tool list. Select Reconnect from /mcp . If the count stays at zero, run claude --debug=mcp and read the server’s stderr in the debug log at ~/.claude/debug/<session-id>.txt .

title: "Debug your configuration - Claude Code Docs"
heading: ​ Check hooks
text:
## ​ Check hooks
- The hook is defined in a standalone file. Hooks go under the "hooks" key in a settings file .
- The matcher value is an array instead of a single string. Claude Code lists the entry as an invalid setting when you start an interactive session and in claude doctor . If the array is under PreToolUse or PermissionRequest , none of that file’s other hooks load either.
- The matcher field is a single string that uses | to match multiple tool names, for example "Edit|Write" . A , separator is equivalent, so "Edit,Write" matches the same tools. Before v2.1.191, a comma fell through to regex evaluation and the matcher never matched, so use | if you aren’t on v2.1.191 yet.
- A misspelled tool name produces a matcher that matches nothing, so the hook fails silently.

- Skills, plugins, and hooks

- Custom output styles

Start Claude Code with a clean configuration directory

Reproduce the problem
- Problem gone : the cause is in your user or project configuration. Copy ~/.claude.json and the files in ~/.claude into ~/claude-clean/config one at a time. If none brings the problem back, go to your project directory in the same shell and start Claude Code without --setting-sources user . In Bash or Zsh, run CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=~/claude-clean/config claude . In PowerShell, the variable is still set, so run claude .
- Problem persists : the cause is outside your user and project configuration. Run /status in the session to check for managed settings, check your shell for environment variables , then see Troubleshooting .

title: "Debug your configuration - Claude Code Docs"
heading: ​ Check common causes
text:
## ​ Check common causes
| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
| Hook never fires | matcher is a JSON array instead of a string | Use a single string with | to match multiple tools, for example "Edit|Write" . See matcher patterns . |
| Hook never fires | matcher uses , as a separator on a version before v2.1.191 | Claude Code v2.1.191 or later treats , as a list separator like | . Earlier versions evaluate a comma as a literal character, so "Edit,Write" matches nothing. Use | instead, or upgrade Claude Code. |
| Hook never fires | matcher value is lowercase, for example "bash" | Matching is case-sensitive. Tool names are capitalized: Bash , Edit , Write , Read . |
| Hook never fires | Hooks are defined in a standalone file instead of settings.json | There is no standalone hooks file for project or user config. Define hooks under the "hooks" key in settings.json . Only plugins load a separate hooks/hooks.json . See hook configuration . |
| Permissions or hooks set globally are ignored | Configuration was added to ~/.claude.json | ~/.claude.json holds app state and UI toggles. permissions , hooks , and env belong in ~/.claude/settings.json . These are two different files. |
| A settings.json value seems ignored | The same key is set in settings.local.json | settings.local.json overrides settings.json , and both override ~/.claude/settings.json . See settings precedence . |
| Skill doesn’t appear in /skills | Skill file is at .claude/skills/name.md instead of in a folder | Use a folder with SKILL.md inside: .claude/skills/name/SKILL.md . |
| Skill appears in /skills but Claude never invokes it | Skill has disable-model-invocation: true in its frontmatter, or its description doesn’t match how you phrase the request | Check the badge in /skills : a “user-only” label means Claude won’t trigger it on its own. See skill invocation . |

title: "Debug your configuration - Claude Code Docs"
heading: ​ Check common causes
text:
| Subdirectory CLAUDE.md instructions seem ignored | Subdirectory files load on demand, not at session start | To load a subdirectory’s CLAUDE.md , ask Claude to read another file in that subdirectory. See when subdirectory files load . |
| Subagent ignores CLAUDE.md instructions | The built-in Explore and Plan agents skip CLAUDE.md at startup. A custom subagent loads it the same way the main conversation does, unless it has omitClaudeMd set in its definition | For Explore or Plan, restate the instruction in your delegating prompt. For a subagent that sets omitClaudeMd , remove the field. For any other custom subagent, put critical instructions in the agent file body, which becomes the agent’s system prompt. See what loads at startup . |
| Cleanup logic never runs at session end | No SessionEnd hook configured | Add a SessionEnd hook in settings.json . See the hook events list . |
| MCP servers in .mcp.json never load | File is under .claude/ , or its servers sit under a top-level servers key, as in VS Code’s mcp.json , instead of mcpServers | Project MCP config goes at the repository root as .mcp.json , not inside .claude/ , with servers under the mcpServers key. See MCP configuration . |
| MCP servers added under mcpServers in settings.json never appear | settings.json does not read an mcpServers key | Define project servers in .mcp.json at the repository root, or run claude mcp add --scope user for user-scoped servers. See MCP configuration . |
| Project MCP server added but doesn’t appear | The one-time approval prompt was dismissed | Project-scoped servers require approval. Run /mcp to see status and approve. |
| MCP server fails to start from some directories | command or args uses a relative file path | Use absolute paths for local scripts. Executables on your PATH like npx or uvx work as-is. |

title: "Debug your configuration - Claude Code Docs"
heading: ​ Check common causes
text:
| MCP server starts without expected environment variables | The server’s config entry doesn’t set them, and they aren’t in the environment Claude Code passes to stdio servers: its own environment, minus the variables it strips from subprocesses | Set per-server env inside the server’s .mcp.json entry, which doesn’t depend on the launch environment or workspace trust. |
| Bash(rm *) deny rule doesn’t block /bin/rm or find -delete | Bash rules match the literal command string, not the underlying executable; see what a Bash rule doesn’t match | Use a PreToolUse hook or the sandbox for a hard guarantee. |

title: "Launch sessions from links - Claude Code Docs"
heading: ​ How deep links work
text:
## ​ How deep links work
- The browser or app passes the URL to your operating system.
- The operating system recognizes the claude-cli:// prefix and starts Claude Code on your machine.
- A new terminal window opens with Claude Code running in the directory the link specified, and the link’s prompt text already in the input box.
- You read the prompt, edit it if you want, and press Enter to send it.

title: "Launch sessions from links - Claude Code Docs"
heading: ​ Build a link
text:
## ​ Build a link

```
claude-cli://open
```
| Parameter | Description |
| q | Text to pre-fill in the prompt box. URL-encode the value. Use %0A for line breaks in multi-line prompts. Maximum 5,000 characters. |
| cwd | Absolute path to use as the working directory. Network and UNC paths are rejected, and so are paths that contain .. segments or invisible or bidirectional control characters. |
| repo | A GitHub owner/name slug. Claude Code resolves it to a local clone it has seen before and starts there. If you have no matching clone, the session opens in your home directory instead. |

```
claude-cli://open?repo=acme/payments&q=Investigate%20the%20failed%20deploy%20of%20payments-api.%0ACheck%20recent%20commits%20to%20main%20and%20the%20last%20successful%20build.
```

```
Investigate the failed deploy of payments-api.


Check recent commits to main and the last successful build.
```

title: "Launch sessions from links - Claude Code Docs"
heading: ​ Choose between cwd and repo
text:
### ​ Choose between cwd and repo
- repo opens the linked repository’s clone or worktree where you most recently ran claude . Each time you run claude in a Git repository, Claude Code records that directory’s path against the repository’s GitHub owner/name slug. Claude Code tracks clones and worktrees separately.
- The link does not change which branch is checked out. The session opens in whatever state that directory is currently in.

text:

2.

title: "Desktop application - Claude Code Docs"
heading: Get Claude for Linux (beta)
text:
## Get Claude for Linux (beta)
- Review and comment on diffs , then watch the resulting PR through CI
- Preview your running app in the Browser pane while Claude verifies its own changes, and open external sites alongside it
- Watch Claude run and test your iOS app in the iOS Simulator pane
- Arrange panes for the chat, diff, browser, terminal, and file editor side by side
- Ask a side question that uses the session’s context without derailing it
- Let Claude check on, message, or archive your other sessions
- Connect external tools like GitHub, Slack, and Linear
- Let Claude open apps and control your screen
- Run on your machine, in the cloud , or over SSH

title: "Desktop application - Claude Code Docs"
heading: ​ Start a session
text:
## ​ Start a session
- Environment : use the environment selector, the first control in the row, to choose where Claude runs. See environment configuration . If a new session has no environment selector under the prompt box, follow the earlier layout’s steps .
- Project folder : click the project folder control, next to the environment selector, to choose the folder Claude works in. Cloud session : select repositories instead of a folder Saved local or SSH environment : the environment already holds its folders, so the row shows no project folder control. To change the folders, edit the environment .
- Permission mode : use the mode selector to choose how much autonomy Claude has. You can change the permission mode during the session.
- Model : pick a model from the model picker toward the right end of the row. You can change the model during the session.

title: "Desktop application - Claude Code Docs"
heading: ​ Add files and context to prompts
text:
### ​ Add files and context to prompts
- @mention files : type @ followed by a filename to add a file to the conversation context. In a cloud session : @ can list files only after you send your first message. If @ lists none, send your first message without the file, then @mention the file in your next message.
- Attach files : attach images, PDFs, and other files to your prompt from the + button next to the prompt box, or drag and drop files directly into the prompt. This is useful for sharing screenshots of bugs, design mockups, or reference documents. In a WSL session : if the + menu shows Add image instead of Add files or photos , you can attach only images. To give Claude any other file from the session’s folder, @mention it.

title: "Desktop application - Claude Code Docs"
heading: ​ Choose a permission mode
text:
### ​ Choose a permission mode
| Mode | Settings key | Behavior |
| Manual | default | Claude asks before editing files or running commands. You see a diff and can accept or reject each change. |
| Accept edits | acceptEdits | Claude auto-accepts file edits and common filesystem commands like mkdir , touch , and mv , but still asks before running other terminal commands. Use this when you trust file changes and want faster iteration. |
| Plan | plan | Claude reads files and runs commands to explore, then proposes a plan without editing your source code. Good for complex tasks where you want to review the approach first. |
| Auto | auto | Claude runs without routine prompts; before actions such as shell commands and network requests run, a background classifier checks that they align with your request. Appears when auto mode is available ; there is no separate Settings toggle for it. |
| Bypass permissions | bypassPermissions | Claude runs without permission prompts, except for the actions no mode auto-approves , safety classifiers when Claude acts on external sites , or desktop actions such as deleting a session, though not archiving one . Equivalent to --dangerously-skip-permissions in the CLI. On Pro and Max plans, enable it in your Settings → Claude Code under “Allow bypass permissions mode”; on Team and Enterprise plans there is no Settings toggle, and organization policy controls it instead. Only use this in sandboxed containers or VMs. |

title: "Desktop application - Claude Code Docs"
heading: ​ Browse external sites
text:
### ​ Browse external sites
- Safety classifiers review Claude’s write actions on external pages, such as clicking and typing, in every permission mode. These are the same classifiers auto mode uses, and when they flag an action, you get a permission prompt regardless of mode.
- In permission modes other than Auto and Bypass permissions, a domain allowlist check also applies before Claude navigates to a new site.

title: "Desktop application - Claude Code Docs"
heading: ​ Monitor pull request status
text:
### ​ Monitor pull request status
- Auto-fix : in a local session, Claude also addresses new review comments that someone other than you leaves. The comment’s author has to be the repository’s owner, an organization member, a collaborator, or a GitHub App.
- Merge when ready : turns on GitHub’s auto-merge for the PR. In a local session, Desktop requests a squash merge unless the base branch uses a merge queue. In SSH and WSL sessions : Merge when ready is disabled, so turn on auto-merge for the pull request on GitHub If the repository doesn’t allow auto-merge : Merge when ready doesn’t turn on, so enable auto-merge in your GitHub repository settings first
- Earlier layout : once the session has a pull request, click CI on its status bar.

title: "Desktop application - Claude Code Docs"
heading: ​ Open and edit files
text:
### ​ Open and edit files
- Local sessions : you can edit files inside the session’s working directory, except some view-only ones such as .mcp.json and .claude/settings.json . To change one, open it in another app .
- Cloud, SSH, and WSL sessions : the file pane is view-only, so ask Claude to make edits.

title: "Desktop application - Claude Code Docs"
heading: ​ App permissions
text:
### ​ App permissions
| Tier | What Claude can do | Applies to |
| View only | See the app in screenshots | Browsers, trading platforms |
| Click only | Click and scroll, but not type or use keyboard shortcuts | Terminals, IDEs |
| Full control | Click, type, drag, and use keyboard shortcuts | Everything else |
- Denied apps : add apps here to reject them without prompting. Claude may still affect a denied app indirectly through actions in an allowed app, but it can’t interact with the denied app directly.
- Unhide apps when Claude finishes : when computer use isn’t running in the background, Claude hides your other windows while it works so it interacts with only the approved app. When Claude finishes, hidden windows are restored unless you turn this setting off.

heading: ​ Run a session in its own worktree
text:
#### ​ Run a session in its own worktree

title: "Desktop application - Claude Code Docs"
heading: ​ Add folders to a session
text:

title: "Desktop application - Claude Code Docs"
heading: ​ Keep uncommitted changes when a session is archived
text:
#### ​ Keep uncommitted changes when a session is archived
- If Desktop asks about the changes : select Archive anyway to discard them, or cancel and commit them
- If the only changes are untracked files : commit the ones you want to keep before a pull request that Claude opened in the session merges, because Desktop can then delete them without asking
- In any other case : the worktree stays on disk with its changes. For a local session, Desktop removes both about 30 days after the session is archived or you last open it, whichever is later. To keep the changes, open the session from the Archived tab and select Unarchive

title: "Desktop application - Claude Code Docs"
heading: ​ Organize and find sessions
text:
### ​ Organize and find sessions
- Current layout : hover over a heading in the session list to show the Group and sort icon, then click it. To find archived sessions, select View all , the menu’s last row, then open the Archived tab.
- Earlier layout : the Filter icon shows without hovering. Click it to arrange the list with Group by or Sort by . To show archived sessions, select Status , then Archived .

title: "Desktop application - Claude Code Docs"
heading: ​ Work across sessions
text:
### ​ Work across sessions
- You get an approval card before Claude archives a session, except in Auto mode and Bypass permissions mode, where Claude can archive a session without one. To be asked, switch to Manual.
- Through this surface, Claude can’t send cross-session messages from a session nobody is watching, such as a scheduled-task run, and can’t deliver messages into one.
- Claude Code checks each message from this surface against the receiving session’s inbound controls , even when the receiving session doesn’t have cross-session messaging itself. If you set crossSessionInbound to refuse in the receiving session, Claude Code drops messages from this surface. Claude Code reports the refusal to the Claude desktop app. Before v2.1.234, Claude Code dropped every message from this surface to a receiving session without cross-session messaging.
- Claude Code quotes each incoming message and attributes it to the session that sent it, and Claude still follows the receiving session’s own permission settings when acting on one.

title: "Desktop application - Claude Code Docs"
heading: ​ Continue in another surface
text:
### ​ Continue in another surface
- Select Cloud to continue the session as a cloud session , with your conversation carried over as a summary. Before you confirm, the dialog states whether your files move too and whether this session is archived once the cloud one is ready. You can’t move a session that runs over SSH or in WSL this way.
- Select an installed editor or your file manager to open the session’s folder on disk there.

title: "Desktop application - Claude Code Docs"
heading: ​ Control which sessions appear on your other devices
text:
### ​ Control which sessions appear on your other devices
- You turn it on for that session : with the session’s Remote Control switch, or by typing /remote-control in its prompt box.
- It connects when it starts : new sessions connect automatically while Connect new sessions to Remote Control is on in Settings > Claude Code . If you’ve never changed that setting, Desktop follows remoteControlAtStartup in your user or managed settings, then your organization’s default.
- One session : turn off its Remote Control switch. In a session that connected when it started, typing /remote-control leaves Remote Control on and shows Remote Control is already on. This session connected automatically when it started. Click Turn off on that line to disconnect.
- New Desktop sessions on this computer : turn off Connect new sessions to Remote Control in Settings > Claude Code . If it already shows off, turn it on and then off so Desktop saves your choice. Once saved, it takes precedence over remoteControlAtStartup and the defaults.
- Any session on this computer, including the CLI : set disableRemoteControl to true in ~/.claude/settings.json to stop sessions from connecting. A session that was already connected when you saved the file stays connected until you turn Remote Control off for it.

text:
#### ​ Configuration fields
| Field | Type | Description |
| name | string | A unique identifier for this server |
| runtimeExecutable | string | The command to run, such as npm , yarn , or node |
| runtimeArgs | string[] | Arguments passed to runtimeExecutable , such as ["run", "dev"] |
| port | number | The port your server listens on. Defaults to 3000 |
| cwd | string | Working directory relative to your project root. Defaults to the project root. Use ${workspaceFolder} to reference the project root explicitly |
| env | object | Additional environment variables as key-value pairs, such as { "NODE_ENV": "development" } . Don’t put secrets here since this file is committed to your repo. For secrets, see Set environment variables for dev servers . |
| autoPort | boolean | How to handle port conflicts. See Port conflicts |
| program | string | A script to run with node . See when to use program vs runtimeExecutable |
| args | string[] | Arguments passed to program . Only used when program is set |
| url | string | The address the preview opens instead of http://localhost:<port> . See open the preview at a specific URL |

title: "Desktop application - Claude Code Docs"
heading: ​ Port conflicts
text:
#### ​ Port conflicts
- true : Claude finds and uses a free port automatically. Suitable for most dev servers.
- false : Claude fails with an error. Use this when your server must use a specific port, such as for OAuth callbacks or CORS allowlists.
- Not set (default) : your server gets the next free port, as with true , except in the one case below. Before Claude Desktop v2.37337.0, Claude asks whether the server needs that exact port instead, then saves your answer in launch.json .
- You start the server through an npm , yarn , pnpm , or bun script.
- Your preferred port is hardcoded in that script, or Claude can’t inspect the script.
- You don’t pass the port in runtimeArgs .

title: "Desktop application - Claude Code Docs"
heading: ​ Environment configuration
text:
## ​ Environment configuration
- Local : runs on your machine with direct access to your files
- Cloud : runs on Anthropic-managed infrastructure by default. Sessions continue even if you close the app.
- SSH : runs on a remote machine you connect to over SSH, such as your own servers, cloud VMs, or dev containers. A running task can keep going while Desktop is disconnected , but with a Claude account it can stop when its sign-in expires.
- WSL (Windows): runs inside a WSL 2 distribution on your machine, using its Linux toolchain and native paths

title: "Desktop application - Claude Code Docs"
heading: ​ Use, edit, or remove a saved environment
text:
#### ​ Use, edit, or remove a saved environment
- Start a session : select the entry.
- Edit or delete : hover over the entry and click the gear icon. To delete a local or SSH environment, click Delete environment in Edit environment .
- Archive cloud environments : see Archive an environment .

title: "Desktop application - Claude Code Docs"
heading: ​ Set environment variables for dev servers
text:
#### ​ Set environment variables for dev servers
- macOS and Linux : export it in your shell profile
- Windows : add it to your user or system environment variables
- Any platform : save it in the local environment editor , if you can open it

heading: ​ Use the local environment editor
text:

- Selector above the prompt box : hover over Local and click the gear icon

title: "Desktop application - Claude Code Docs"
heading: ​ Environment variables Desktop sets itself
text:
#### ​ Environment variables Desktop sets itself
- API_TIMEOUT_MS : a local session gets 900000 , which is 15 minutes. For a longer timeout, install the Claude Code CLI and use it instead of Desktop. Set the variable in your shell and run claude in your terminal.
- ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL : a local session gets Anthropic’s API host when you’re signed in with a Claude account. To use a gateway, set up Desktop’s third-party inference configuration instead.

title: "Desktop application - Claude Code Docs"
heading: ​ Cloud sessions

### ​ Cloud sessions
- Add an environment : select New environment at the bottom of the selector’s menu, then the Cloud tab of the New environment dialog

title: "Desktop application - Claude Code Docs"
heading: ​ SSH sessions
text:
### ​ SSH sessions
Open the New environment dialog
Add the connection
- Name : a friendly label for this connection.
- SSH host : user@hostname or a host defined in ~/.ssh/config .
- SSH port : defaults to 22 if left empty, or uses the port from your SSH config.
- SSH key (optional) : path to your private key, such as ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 . Leave empty to use your SSH config or SSH agent.
- Worktree folder : a folder on the remote machine, such as ~/worktrees , where new sessions create their worktrees. Leave empty to use the remote machine’s default .
Start a session on the connection

title: "Desktop application - Claude Code Docs"
heading: ​ Remote machine requirements for SSH sessions
text:
#### ​ Remote machine requirements for SSH sessions
- System : an x86_64 or arm64 processor. The machine also has to meet Claude Code’s system requirements . On Linux, Claude Code needs glibc 2.17 or later, or musl. To see which one the machine has, run ldd --version there. On a musl-based distribution such as Alpine Linux, also install the packages that Claude Code needs .
- SFTP : the SSH server has to offer the SFTP subsystem, which a Subsystem sftp line in its sshd_config turns on. To check, connect to the same host and port with sftp in a terminal on your computer. A working server shows the sftp> prompt.
- Sessions per connection : Desktop on macOS and Linux opens several sessions on one SSH connection. If the server’s sshd_config sets MaxSessions 1 , raise it, for example to OpenSSH’s default of 10.
- Install folder : Desktop installs a helper program and Claude Code under ~/.claude/remote/ in your home directory. It runs them from there, so that folder can’t be on a file system mounted noexec . Allow about 1 GB of disk space in the home directory of each user who connects. For what that folder holds, see Files and processes on the remote machine .
- Shell : the shell set for your account on the remote machine has to run commands sent over SSH, as Bash, Zsh, and sh do
- Network : Claude Code runs on the remote machine and makes its network requests from there, so the machine needs the network access that Claude Code requires . If the machine can’t download Claude Code, Desktop downloads it on your computer and uploads it. Claude Code’s other requests still go out from the remote machine. On a Linux remote machine, if those requests need a proxy, set it for SSH sessions .

title: "Desktop application - Claude Code Docs"

Add the variables

```
{


  "env"

"http://proxy.example.com:8080"

Give sessions the new value

title: "Desktop application - Claude Code Docs"
heading: ​ Use your SSH configuration on macOS and Linux
text:
#### ​ Use your SSH configuration on macOS and Linux
- Client version : run ssh -V . The client has to be OpenSSH 7.6 or later.
- Entry : run ssh with the Host name, such as ssh devbox . If that fails, fix the entry first.
- SSH port : a value here overrides the entry’s Port
- SSH key (optional) : Desktop offers the key file you pick in addition to the entry’s IdentityFile and the keys in your SSH agent

```
Host devbox


  HostName devbox.internal.example.com


  User alice


  ProxyJump bastion.example.com
```
Add the entry

```
Host devbox-container


  User dev


  ProxyCommand ssh build.example.com docker exec -i devbox /usr/sbin/sshd -i
```
Prepare the container
- Install the OpenSSH server, with a host key that stays the same when you rebuild the image or recreate the container
- Give the account named in User a way to log in, such as an authorized_keys file
- Check that the container meets the remote machine requirements
Check the allowlist
Test the entry, then connect
- If ssh asks for a password, passphrase, or code : switch to a login that works without a prompt, such as a key that your SSH agent holds
- If ssh reports Cannot execute command-line and remote command. or Bad packet length : take RemoteCommand and RequestTTY out of your entry for build.example.com . After that, ssh build.example.com in a terminal on your computer opens a shell on that machine, not in the container.
- If ssh reports Connection closed by UNKNOWN port 65535 : run ssh build.example.com docker exec devbox /usr/sbin/sshd -t in the same terminal. If it prints Missing privilege separation directory: /run/sshd , create that folder in the container. If it prints no hostkeys available and the container has host keys, add -u root after exec in this command and in the entry.
Add a profile with a region and a source of credentials

title: "Desktop application - Claude Code Docs"
heading: ​ Use your SSH configuration on macOS and Linux
text:
```
[profile corp]


region
 = us-east-1


credential_process
 = /full/path/to/your-credential-helper
```
- region : give the AWS Region of the machines you connect to
- credential_process : give the full path of a program that prints credentials in the JSON form that AWS documents . Choose a program that needs no input from you, because the AWS CLI runs it at every connection, including reconnects while you’re away.
- IAM Identity Center : add the profile’s IAM Identity Center settings in place of credential_process . Run aws sso login --profile corp in a terminal before you connect, and again when that sign-in lapses.
Name the profile in the ProxyCommand

```
Host i-*


  ProxyCommand sh -c "aws ssm start-session --profile corp --target %h --document-name AWS-StartSSHSession --parameters 'portNumber=%p'"
```
Connect again

```
Host devbox


  HostName devbox.internal.example.com


  User alice


  ProxyJump bastion.example.com


  ConnectTimeout 120
```

```
ssh
 -G
 -o
 HostName=devbox.internal.example.com
 -l
 alice
 devbox
```

```
Match host *.internal.example.com !originalhost devbox
```
- To reach a port on the remote machine : forward it yourself
- To use your own keys from the remote machine : set up a credential on the remote machine itself, for example for git push

title: "Desktop application - Claude Code Docs"
heading: ​ Windows remote machines
text:
#### ​ Windows remote machines
- Terminal : the terminal doesn’t open in a session whose folder is a Windows path, such as C:/projects/app
- Sandbox : Claude Code runs there on native Windows, where it runs commands unsandboxed. See where the sandbox runs .
- Plugins : Desktop doesn’t copy a plugin that holds a file or folder name Windows can’t store, such as a name with : . The session lists the plugins that Desktop left out.
- MCP servers : on some Windows remote machines, Claude’s calls to MCP servers from claude_desktop_config.json go through Desktop, so Claude can’t call their tools while Desktop is disconnected . Before Claude Desktop v2.37337.0, this holds on every Windows remote machine.
- Worktrees : worktrees go in <project-root>/.claude/worktrees/ . If you choose another folder , Desktop ignores it.
- Earlier messages : if the SSH server’s shell is cmd.exe or Windows PowerShell, you may have to connect before you see a session’s earlier messages
- Forks : if the SSH server’s shell is cmd.exe or Windows PowerShell, you can fork a session only at its first message
- Running while disconnected : a task keeps running while Desktop is disconnected only if the SSH server lets a program outlive the connection that started it. To find out, test the remote machine .
- Leftover processes : after a session ends, check the machine for programs that Claude Code started, because they can keep running. The background helper that Desktop installs doesn’t stop on its own there.

title: "Desktop application - Claude Code Docs"
heading: ​ Keep a task running while Desktop is disconnected
text:
#### ​ Keep a task running while Desktop is disconnected
- Keep your computer awake and online, with the lid open and Desktop running
- Use a login that works without a prompt, such as a key that your SSH agent holds, for the remote machine and for any jump host on the way. Desktop can then reconnect on its own after a drop.
- After sleep or a network loss : you get the running task back if the process still runs and Desktop can log in without a prompt. If it can’t, send a message .
- After a quit : the task keeps running, but you lose it when the session opens again unless Desktop can rejoin its process. Check when Desktop can rejoin before you quit. If you lost the task, send a message to continue.
- Desktop can’t reconnect : the session says why, and a notification may say so too. Desktop may need you to log in .
- Authentication error : the sign-in token or credential may have expired. With a Claude account, send a message to continue. With a third-party provider, see SSH remote sessions in Claude Desktop on 3P .
- Waiting request : answer it
- None of these : send a message to continue
- Update first : update Desktop before you start a long task. On macOS and Windows, Desktop can restart on its own to install an update that it has downloaded. That restart waits while Claude is working on an SSH task. On macOS with a Claude account, by default the restart can go ahead anyway once the update has waited 72 hours.
- Don’t quit on Windows, or before v2.42304.0 with a third-party provider : after a quit there you lose the running task, so leave Desktop open during the task. In any other case, see what you get back before you quit.
- Reduce requests : choose a permission mode, rules, or hooks that make the task wait for you less often
- Check the jump host : if your jump host asks for a sign-in, for example a push to a phone, switch to a login that works without a prompt. Otherwise Desktop can send another push each time it tries to reconnect.

title: "Desktop application - Claude Code Docs"
heading: ​ Keep a task running while Desktop is disconnected
text:
- Test the remote machine : start a short task, quit Desktop while the task is still running, and open the session again well after the task should be done. If the task isn’t finished and the session shows no authentication error, check the remote machine for what can end a task .
- Keep commands out of Desktop’s terminal : if the remote machine logs out idle terminals , run your own commands from an SSH login outside Desktop
- Sign-in token or credential : with a Claude account, the task stops with an authentication error when the token expires. With a third-party provider, the same holds for a credential that expires, such as one from single sign-on or a credential helper. See SSH remote sessions in Claude Desktop on 3P . With a Claude account, keep Desktop running and connected so that it can renew the sign-in.
- The remote machine : if the remote machine restarts, or ends your processes when your SSH connection closes, the running task ends. Nothing starts it again while Desktop is disconnected. Linux machines where systemd-logind’s KillUserProcesses is yes and applies to your user end your processes this way. To keep a task running there, ask the administrator to exempt your user, for example with KillExcludeUsers .
- Idle terminals : some Linux remote machines log out a terminal that nobody types in for a set time (systemd-logind’s StopIdleSessionSec ). With Desktop on macOS or Linux, a session’s terminal and ! commands share Desktop’s SSH connection by default. That logout then ends the connection while Desktop is connected, and the running task can end with it. Closing the terminal pane doesn’t prevent it, so keep commands out of that terminal .
- Desktop updates : if an update brings a new helper, Desktop replaces the helper on the remote machine at a later connection, which can end a task that still runs

title: "Desktop application - Claude Code Docs"
heading: ​ Keep a task running while Desktop is disconnected
text:
- Long absences : on a Linux or macOS remote machine, if Desktop doesn’t connect for 30 days, the helper stops and ends every Claude Code process that runs under it. Connect before then.
- Worktrees : in a session that uses a worktree , Desktop checks each file edit before Claude makes it. While Desktop is disconnected, each edit waits about 30 seconds and then fails. Shell commands still run. On a Linux or macOS remote machine, edits can keep working . If you aren’t sure, start the session without a worktree.
- Folder restrictions : if your organization restricts which folders sessions may use, Desktop checks each file read, search, and edit, with or without a worktree. While Desktop is disconnected, each one waits up to 10 minutes and then fails.
- Connectors : connectors and other tools that Desktop provides run through Desktop, so while it is disconnected each call fails after about 30 seconds
- Workflows : Desktop checks each new workflow before it starts, so while Desktop is disconnected a new one waits up to 10 minutes and then fails
- MCP servers : MCP servers that Claude Code starts on the remote machine don’t run through Desktop, so Claude can still call their tools. Servers from claude_desktop_config.json are among them only if Desktop doesn’t use its built-in SSH client . Otherwise, and on some Windows remote machines , Claude can’t call their tools while Desktop is disconnected.
When edits in a worktree keep working
- Built-in SSH client : Desktop uses it, for example in a Microsoft Store install, on a Windows computer without Microsoft’s OpenSSH 9.4 or later, or by default on Windows with a third-party provider
- Repository location : the repository is your home directory, a folder above it, or ~/.claude
- macOS paths : on a macOS remote machine, the repository is under /Volumes , or a folder name in the path of the repository or the worktree has a ~ or a non-ASCII character

title: "Desktop application - Claude Code Docs"
heading: ​ Keep a task running while Desktop is disconnected
text:
- Folder restrictions : your organization restricts which folders sessions may use
- Corporate launcher : before Claude Desktop v2.37337.0, you sign in with a Claude account, and your organization starts Claude Code on the remote machine through a corporate launcher
- Auto mode : choose Auto mode if it is available to you . After repeated blocks, you are asked again .
- Allow rules : in your user settings file on the remote machine, ~/.claude/settings.json , add allow rules for the commands the task needs. If your organization accepts permission rules from managed settings only , ask your administrator to add them to the managed settings that reach the remote machine. For allow rules in a project’s .claude/settings.json , see Project allow rules and workspace trust .
- A hook that answers : configure a PermissionRequest hook in ~/.claude/settings.json on the remote machine to allow or deny requests in your place
- A hook that alerts you : configure a Notification hook with the permission_prompt matcher in the same file to send yourself a message when a request is waiting
- A hook that tells you when Claude is done : configure a Stop hook in the same file to send yourself a message when Claude has finished responding. It doesn’t run when an API error ends the turn. For that case, configure a StopFailure hook .
- Remembered password : a password that you let Desktop remember also works without a prompt, but for a long absence prefer a key that your SSH agent holds. If sign-ins with that password break off or hang, Desktop can stop reconnecting and wait for you.
- Any other prompt : if the remote machine prompts for anything else, such as a one-time code, you can get a notification on your computer. Click the notification, or send a message in the session, and Desktop shows the prompt.

title: "Desktop application - Claude Code Docs"
heading: ​ Keep a task running while Desktop is disconnected
text:
If a jump host asks for a sign-in, the outage is long, output is missing, or the process is gone
- Jump host, pushes stop while you’re away : this can happen with Desktop on macOS or Linux when nobody answers a jump host’s sign-in, for example a push to a phone. Desktop then stops reconnecting while nobody is at your computer. When you unlock or use the computer, you can get another push, because Desktop can try again. After three unanswered attempts it waits until you retry or send a message.
- Jump host, pushes keep coming : where Desktop can’t tell that nobody answers, as with Desktop on Windows, it keeps trying while it has a process to rejoin, whether or not that process still runs. You can get another push with each attempt. To end the attempts, quit Desktop, which can cost you the running task .
- Long outage : Desktop slows to about one attempt every five minutes. To reconnect sooner, retry in the session or send a message, which Desktop delivers once it is connected.
- Missing output : while Desktop is disconnected, the helper keeps each session’s most recent Claude Code output in a 16 MiB buffer and drops older output. After Desktop reconnects, the session can show Loading recent output from <host>… . If Desktop can’t load all of the output, you see the row Some output produced while you were disconnected may be missing here. The row doesn’t mean that the task stopped.
- Process gone : the process ended while Desktop was disconnected, as when the remote machine restarts. Desktop can then start a new one from the conversation’s saved history and tell Claude to continue the task. If the task stays stopped, send a message. With a third-party provider, update to Claude Desktop v2.42304.0 or later, because earlier versions never continue the task on their own.
- Desktop on Windows : you don’t get the running task back, because Desktop never rejoins after a quit. Start Desktop again only when you expect the task to be done, because the session can open as Desktop starts.

title: "Desktop application - Claude Code Docs"
heading: ​ Keep a task running while Desktop is disconnected
text:
- Third-party provider, task from an earlier version : if you started the task in a Desktop version before v2.42304.0, you don’t get it back on macOS or Linux either. Start Desktop again only when you expect the task to be done.
- Any other task, with Desktop on macOS or Linux : start Desktop and open the session, and the task goes on if Desktop rejoins. It can’t always rejoin, for example after some Desktop updates, so update before a long task .

title: "Desktop application - Claude Code Docs"
heading: ​ Connections that close before login
text:
#### ​ Connections that close before login
| OpenSSH version | Lines for a test | Lines if the greeting arrives first |
| 6.6 to 7.9 | A line with Did not receive identification string from 203.0.113.7 | The same line |
| 8.0 to 8.2 | error: kex_exchange_identification: Connection closed by remote host | error: kex_exchange_identification: read: Connection reset by peer |
| 8.3 to 9.4 | error: kex_exchange_identification: Connection closed by remote host , then Connection closed by 203.0.113.7 port 51234 | error: kex_exchange_identification: read: Connection reset by peer , then Connection reset by 203.0.113.7 port 51234 |
| 9.5 to 10.2 | Connection closed by 203.0.113.7 port 51234 | error: kex_exchange_identification: read: Connection reset by peer , then Connection reset by 203.0.113.7 port 51234 |
| 10.3 to 10.5 | Connection closed by 203.0.113.7 port 51234 [preauth] | error: kex_exchange_identification: read: Connection reset by peer [preauth] , then Connection reset by 203.0.113.7 port 51234 [preauth] |

```
drop connection #0 from [203.0.113.7]:51234 on [192.0.2.10]:22 penalty: connections without attempting authentication
```
- A filter line that names a mode in brackets , such as filter = sshd[mode=aggressive] : use that mode.
- Only the stock filter line , with [mode=%(mode)s] : use the mode line, or normal if there is none.

```
fail2ban-regex
 -o
 ip
 lines.log
 "sshd[mode=aggressive]"
```
- mode : set it to normal wherever your jail sets it, in a mode line or in the brackets of a line such as filter = sshd[mode=aggressive] . You give up every count that only the other modes make, for example of clients that connect and leave without trying to log in.
- ignoreip : set it to the addresses that people connect from, for example ignoreip = 203.0.113.7 . fail2ban then counts nothing from those addresses, failed logins included.

title: "Desktop application - Claude Code Docs"
heading: ​ Open an SSH session from a link
text:
#### ​ Open an SSH session from a link

```
claude://code/new?ssh_host=dev%40build.example.com&ssh_port=2222&ssh_folder=/srv/payments&q=Investigate%20the%20failed%20deploy
```
| Parameter | Value |
| ssh_host | host or user@host , written as in the SSH host field. The value can’t start with - , and the host part takes only letters, digits, . , _ , : , and - |
| ssh_port | A port number from 1 to 65535 |
| ssh_folder | A folder on the remote machine. Start it with / or ~/ , or use ~ |
| q | URL-encoded text for the prompt box |
- A connection you already have : if the host, user, and port match one of your connections, Desktop asks whether to use it, and shows you the connection’s name and host, and the folder if the link names one.
- A new connection : otherwise Desktop opens the dialog for adding an SSH connection. When you add the connection, Desktop asks whether to connect before it saves anything, and shows you the host from the link, and the port and folder if the link names them.
- Before you confirm : check the host and folder.
- Before you send : check the prompt and the selected environment.
- You’re signed out : sign in, then open the link again.
- Another dialog is open : close it, then open the link again.
- The link isn’t valid : Desktop shows a message that says what to fix, and doesn’t fill in the prompt.
- Desktop is older than v2.110.0 : earlier versions ignore the SSH parameters and open the new-session page with only the prompt.
- SSH sessions are turned off : if your administrator sets the allowlist to an empty array, Desktop refuses SSH links.

true

: 
"shared-dev-vm"

"Shared Dev VM"

- The CLI : none of the keys stops a developer from running the Claude Code CLI on their own computer
- Cowork : none of the keys applies to Cowork sessions or Cowork scheduled tasks
- Cloud sessions : none of the keys changes whether cloud sessions are available. To turn them off, use the Cloud sessions setting under Admin console controls .
- Hostnames : make sure that a pattern in sshHostAllowlist matches the hostname of each sshConfigs entry, without user@ , or developers can’t connect to it. For how Desktop matches a hostname, see Restrict which SSH hosts users can connect to .
- Version : disableDesktopLocalSessions requires Claude Desktop v1.37937.0 or later
- File permissions : make sure that each developer’s account on the computer can read the managed settings file. Desktop doesn’t apply the keys in a file that the account can’t read, and Claude Code starts without them too.
Check the environment selector

- Shared Dev VM under SSH . If it isn’t listed there, click the single SSH row, or More at the end of the group.

- Managed settings file : make sure that the file is valid JSON.
- Managed source : make sure that the computer reads the managed source that holds the keys.

title: "Desktop application - Claude Code Docs"
heading: ​ Admin console controls
text:
### ​ Admin console controls
- Desktop : control whether users in your organization can access Claude Code in the desktop app
- Cloud sessions : enable or disable cloud sessions for your organization
- Remote Control : enable or disable Remote Control for your organization

title: "Desktop application - Claude Code Docs"
heading: ​ Managed settings
text:
### ​ Managed settings
| Key | Description |
| permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode | set to "disable" to prevent users from enabling Bypass permissions mode. |
| disableAutoMode | set to "disable" to remove Auto mode from the mode selector. Also accepted under permissions . |
| autoMode | customize what the auto mode classifier trusts and blocks across your organization. See Configure auto mode . |
| browserExternalPageTools | set to "disabled" to prevent Claude from using tools to read or act on external pages in the Browser pane . Users can still navigate to external sites themselves, and local dev server previews are unaffected. |
| disableMobileSimulatorTools | set to true to block Claude’s tools for controlling and capturing devices in the iOS Simulator pane . The pane stays usable for the user’s own taps; only Claude’s access is removed. The value must be the JSON boolean true ; the string "true" is ignored. |
| disableBrowserExternalNavigation | set to true to turn off external browsing in the Browser pane entirely. Neither users nor Claude can navigate to external sites, and localhost dev server previews are unaffected. The value must be the JSON boolean true ; the string "true" is ignored. |
| sshConfigs | pre-configure SSH connections that appear in the environment selector. Users can’t delete managed connections or edit anything but their own Worktree folder . |
| sshHostAllowlist | restrict SSH sessions to hosts whose resolved hostname matches one of these patterns. Read from managed settings only. |
| disableDesktopLocalSessions | set to true to turn off Code sessions that run on the device , leaving SSH sessions to other hosts and cloud sessions available. The value must be the JSON boolean true . Read from managed settings only. Requires Claude Desktop v1.37937.0 or later. |

title: "Desktop application - Claude Code Docs"
heading: ​ Managed settings
text:
| disableSshSavedPasswords | set to true to stop Desktop from offering to remember SSH passwords and from using or showing the ones it saved earlier. Turning it on doesn’t delete them. Read from managed settings only. Requires Claude Desktop v1.49585.0 or later. |
| managedMcpServers | push MCP server configurations to all users. Available in third-party (3P) Desktop deployments only. In each entry, set a transport of "http" , "sse" , or "stdio" , connection details, and optionally a toolPolicy map to restrict which of that server’s tools users can invoke. Deliver it through the managed settings file, MDM, or a Claude apps gateway policy’s desktop block , since 3P deployments don’t receive admin-console settings. To deliver it through the gateway, you need Claude Code v2.1.232 or later on the gateway server. This is the desktop app’s own key; Claude Code reads a same-named managed setting of its own, with a different entry shape. |
- Local sessions on this machine : a managed settings file deployed to disk applies. Managed settings pushed remotely through the admin console also reach these sessions on Anthropic’s API when the session authenticates with an eligible login , following the same settings precedence as the terminal CLI.
- Cloud sessions : receive server-managed settings ; device-deployed files don’t reach them, because they run on Anthropic-managed VMs. Sessions routed to a self-hosted environment also read the managed settings file in the runner image. How Claude Code combines managed sources says when that file applies.
- SSH sessions : the session reads the managed settings file from the remote host. Desktop itself reads sshConfigs , sshHostAllowlist , disableSshSavedPasswords , and disableDesktopLocalSessions on the local machine. If you deliver more than one managed source, it reads them from one by default .

title: "Desktop application - Claude Code Docs"
heading: ​ Managed settings
text: - Cowork sessions : in a Cowork session on this machine, Claude Code never fetches admin-console settings, even when the user signs in with a Team or Enterprise account, and reads policy deployed to the machine unless your Claude Desktop configuration sets requireCoworkFullVmSandbox . Remote Cowork sessions receive neither. See where and when a policy applies for which device files reach Cowork, and MCP permission rules for how Bash and WebFetch rules apply to Cowork’s tools.

title: "Desktop application - Claude Code Docs"
heading: ​ What’s not available in Desktop
text:
### ​ What’s not available in Desktop
- Third-party providers : Desktop connects to Anthropic’s API by default. To route Desktop through a gateway, or to run the Code tab on Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud’s Agent Platform, Microsoft Foundry, or a self-hosted LLM gateway, follow the links in the Third-party providers row .
- Linux (beta) : Computer Use isn’t yet available in the Linux desktop app. See Claude Desktop on Linux .
- Inline code suggestions : Desktop doesn’t offer autocomplete-style code completions. It works through conversational prompts and explicit code changes, and can suggest your next prompt after Claude replies.
- Agent teams : coordinated teams, where Claude as the team lead assigns tasks to teammates from a shared task list, are available in the CLI , not in Desktop. For multi-agent work inside one session, use dynamic workflows , which run in Desktop; Claude can also message and manage your other sessions directly.
- Terminal-dialog commands : built-in commands that open an interactive panel in the terminal behave differently in the Code tab. Edit settings files directly to manage permission rules and configuration, or run the commands from the standalone CLI. Commands with no argument form, such as /permissions , reply with isn't available in this environment . /config opens Settings → Claude Code. Text after the command is ignored, so /config theme=dark doesn’t set the theme.

title: "Desktop application - Claude Code Docs"
heading: ​ Check which layout you have
text:
### ​ Check which layout you have
- Desktop older than v2.37337.0 : update to get the current layout. Select Claude > Check for Updates… on macOS or Help > Check for Updates… on Windows.
- Third-party provider : you keep the earlier layout, so there is nothing to do.

title: "Desktop application - Claude Code Docs"
heading: ​ 403 or authentication errors in the Code tab
text:
### ​ 403 or authentication errors in the Code tab
- Sign out and back in from the app menu. This is the most common fix.
- Verify you have an active paid subscription: Pro, Max, Team, or Enterprise.
- If the CLI works but Desktop does not, quit the desktop app completely, not just close the window, then reopen and sign in again.
- Check your internet connection and proxy settings.

title: "Desktop application - Claude Code Docs"
heading: ​ Blank or stuck screen on launch
text:
### ​ Blank or stuck screen on launch
- Restart the app.
- Check for pending updates. On macOS and Windows the app auto-updates on launch; on Linux, update through apt as described in Claude Desktop on Linux .
- On a managed network, confirm your firewall allows the CDN hosts in network access requirements .
- On Windows, check Event Viewer for crash logs under Windows Logs → Application .

title: "Desktop application - Claude Code Docs"
heading: ​ SSH connection fails after you log in
text:
### ​ SSH connection fails after you log in
| Title on the card | Code | What to do |
| <host>'s SSH server has SFTP turned off | [SFTP_UNAVAILABLE] | Turn on SFTP in the server’s sshd_config , as described under remote machine requirements |
| SFTP doesn't start on <host> | [SFTP_NOT_STARTED] | Connect to the same host with sftp in a terminal on your computer to see what stops it, then check the settings and files that Desktop’s message names |
| <host> allows too few SSH sessions per connection | [SESSION_LIMIT] | Raise MaxSessions in the server’s sshd_config , for example to OpenSSH’s default of 10 |
| <host> is out of disk space | [ENOSPC] or [EDQUOT] | Free space or quota on the remote machine, in your home directory or /tmp |
| This computer is out of disk space | [ENOSPC] or [EDQUOT] , in a message that starts with Couldn't prepare the deploy locally | Free space on your computer |
| Claude Code won't start on <host> | [CLI_UNRESPONSIVE] | Wait a minute, then try again. If it keeps failing, run the command that the message names on the remote machine to see whether Claude Code answers there. |

### ​ Windows-specific issues
- PATH not updated after install : open a new terminal window. PATH updates only apply to new terminal sessions.
- Concurrent installation error : if you see an error about another installation in progress but there isn’t one, try running the installer as Administrator.

title: "Test iOS apps in the simulator - Claude Code Docs"
heading: ​ Requirements
text:
## ​ Requirements
- Claude Desktop v1.24012.0 or later
- A Mac, since Apple’s iOS Simulator runs only on macOS
- Xcode with the iOS platform installed, which provides the simulator devices. If Xcode lists no simulators yet, see The simulator pane says no simulators were found Xcode 26.x or Xcode 27 is recommended, and the pane works with either. If you have more than one Xcode installed, see Choose which Xcode the simulator pane uses

title: "Test iOS apps in the simulator - Claude Code Docs"
heading: ​ Control the simulator yourself
text:
## ​ Control the simulator yourself
- Tap and swipe by clicking and dragging on the device screen
- Press hardware buttons with the same shortcuts as Apple’s Simulator app: Cmd+Shift+H for Home, Cmd+L to lock, Cmd+Up Arrow and Cmd+Down Arrow for volume
- Rotate the device a quarter turn clockwise with the rotate button or Cmd+Right Arrow
- Switch which device the pane shows from the device menu, which lists each simulator’s OS version and whether it’s booted
- Save a screenshot with Cmd+S or a screen recording with Cmd+R , using the pane’s capture buttons or the shortcuts; the files are saved to your Desktop
- Stop streaming a device without shutting it down by clicking Detach simulator , which returns the pane to its Attach simulator state

title: "Test iOS apps in the simulator - Claude Code Docs"
heading: ​ Actions that follow your permission mode
text:
### ​ Actions that follow your permission mode
- Opening a URL on the device, for example to test a deep link or load a page in the device’s Safari, because a URL can carry data off the device.
- Building the app, because xcodebuild runs your project’s build scripts on your Mac. Checking on a build already in progress doesn’t prompt.

title: "Test iOS apps in the simulator - Claude Code Docs"
heading: ​ Turn off simulator access
text:
### ​ Turn off simulator access
- The disableMobileSimulatorTools managed setting blocks Claude’s simulator tools. The simulator pane stays usable for your own taps, and the setting can’t be overridden from within the app.
- The requireCoworkFullVmSandbox policy key, which runs Claude’s tools inside an isolated virtual machine instead of on your Mac, disables the simulator pane and Claude’s simulator tools entirely, so the pane can’t attach a device while it’s set.

title: "Test iOS apps in the simulator - Claude Code Docs"

title: "Claude Desktop on Linux (beta) - Claude Code Docs"
heading: ​ Cowork requirements
text:
### ​ Cowork requirements
- Hardware virtualization : turned on in your firmware settings. Without it, Cowork reports “Cowork requires hardware virtualization (KVM)”.
- QEMU and UEFI firmware : qemu-system-x86 , ovmf , and virtiofsd on x86_64, or qemu-system-arm , qemu-efi-aarch64 , and virtiofsd on arm64. apt install claude-desktop installs them by default as recommended packages. If you installed with --no-install-recommends , or your system is a minimal image that skips recommended packages, Cowork reports “Cowork requires QEMU” and shows the apt install command to run. Ubuntu 22.04 has no virtiofsd package; the app uses a bundled copy there.
- Access to /dev/kvm : add your user to the kvm group with sudo usermod -aG kvm $USER , then log out and back in. Some desktop environments grant the logged-in user access to /dev/kvm without the group, but Cowork also needs /dev/vhost-vsock , which only kvm group members can open. Join the group even if /dev/kvm already works for you.

title: "Claude Desktop on Linux (beta) - Claude Code Docs"
heading: ​ Unable to locate package claude-desktop
text:
### ​ Unable to locate package claude-desktop
- Run sudo apt update after adding the repository. apt install on its own doesn’t see a repository you added after the last time you ran apt update .
- Confirm the repository entry was written. cat /etc/apt/sources.list.d/claude-desktop.list should show the deb line from the Add Anthropic’s apt repository step. If the file is empty or missing, run that step again.
- Confirm your architecture is supported. dpkg --print-architecture should print amd64 or arm64 . The repository doesn’t publish packages for other architectures.
- Run sudo apt update again and check its output for errors related to downloads.claude.ai . A network or key error there means the repository was added but couldn’t be reached or verified.

title: "Claude Desktop on Linux (beta) - Claude Code Docs"
heading: ​ Unmet dependencies
text:
### ​ Unmet dependencies
- libc6 (>= 2.34) : your distribution is older than the package supports. Ubuntu 20.04 ships libc6 2.31. Upgrade to Ubuntu 22.04 or later, or Debian 12 or later.
- All missing dependencies show not installable with an :amd64 or :arm64 suffix: you downloaded the .deb for a different architecture than your machine’s. Run dpkg --print-architecture and download the matching .deb , or install from the apt repository , which selects the package for your architecture.

title: "Claude Desktop on Linux (beta) - Claude Code Docs"
heading: ​ Your sign-in won’t be saved on this device
text:
### ​ Your sign-in won’t be saved on this device
- No keyring installed, on a desktop other than KDE Plasma : if you installed with --no-install-recommends , or on a minimal image that skips recommended packages, apt didn’t install a keyring. Install GNOME Keyring with sudo apt install gnome-keyring .
- KDE Plasma with GNOME Keyring also installed : KDE Wallet comes with the Plasma desktop. The two keyrings conflict, and Claude Desktop can show this notice even though KDE Wallet works. Remove the extra one with sudo apt remove gnome-keyring , then restart your computer.
- Keyring installed but locked : unlock it.

title: "Claude Desktop on Linux (beta) - Claude Code Docs"
heading: ​ Cowork isn’t available
text:
### ​ Cowork isn’t available
- Cowork requires QEMU : install the QEMU and UEFI firmware packages the message lists.
- Cowork requires hardware virtualization (KVM) : turn on hardware virtualization in your firmware settings.
- Claude doesn’t have permission to use virtualization (/dev/kvm) : add your user to the kvm group , then log out and back in.
- Cowork requires the vhost_vsock kernel module : run sudo modprobe vhost_vsock , then restart the app. That loads the module for the current boot only. To load it on every boot, run echo vhost_vsock | sudo tee /etc/modules-load.d/vhost_vsock.conf .

text:
## ​ Variables
- CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC
- DISABLE_TELEMETRY
- DISABLE_ERROR_REPORTING
- CLAUDE_CODE_TMUX_TRUECOLOR
- IS_DEMO
| Variable | Purpose |
| ANTHROPIC_API_KEY | API key sent as X-Api-Key header. When set, this key is used instead of your Claude Pro, Max, Team, or Enterprise subscription even if you are logged in. In non-interactive mode ( -p ), the key is always used when present. In interactive mode, you are prompted to approve the key once before it overrides your subscription. To use your subscription instead, run unset ANTHROPIC_API_KEY |
| ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN | Custom value for the Authorization header (the value you set here will be prefixed with Bearer ) |
| ANTHROPIC_AWS_API_KEY | Workspace API key for Claude Platform on AWS , generated in the AWS Console. Sent as x-api-key and takes precedence over AWS SigV4 |
| ANTHROPIC_AWS_BASE_URL | Override the Claude Platform on AWS endpoint URL. Use for custom regions or when routing through an LLM gateway . Defaults to https://aws-external-anthropic.{region}.api.aws . Claude Code resolves the region with the same precedence as on Amazon Bedrock |
| ANTHROPIC_AWS_WORKSPACE_ID | Required for Claude Platform on AWS . Sent on every request as the anthropic-workspace-id header |
| ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL | Override the API endpoint to route requests through a proxy or gateway. For what happens when that gateway rejects MCP tool search, see Tool search through an LLM gateway . As of v2.1.196, Remote Control is disabled when this points at a host other than api.anthropic.com , matching its behavior on Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud’s Agent Platform, and Microsoft Foundry |
| ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_BASE_URL | Override the Amazon Bedrock endpoint URL. Use for custom Amazon Bedrock endpoints or when routing through an LLM gateway . See Amazon Bedrock |

title: "Environment variables - Claude Code Docs"
heading: ​ Variables
text:
| ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_MANTLE_BASE_URL | Override the Amazon Bedrock Mantle endpoint URL. See Mantle endpoint |
| ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_REGION_PREFIX | Cross-region inference profile prefix ( us , eu , apac , jp , au , or global ) Claude Code tries first instead of the one derived from the AWS region. Ignored in AWS GovCloud regions. Requires Claude Code v2.1.224 or later. See Amazon Bedrock |
| ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_SERVICE_TIER | Amazon Bedrock service tier ( default , flex , or priority ). Sent as the X-Amzn-Bedrock-Service-Tier header. See Amazon Bedrock |
| ANTHROPIC_BETAS | Comma-separated list of additional anthropic-beta header values to include in API requests. Claude Code already sends the beta headers it needs; use this to opt into an Anthropic API beta before Claude Code adds native support. Unlike the --betas flag , which requires API key authentication, this variable works with all auth methods including Claude.ai subscription |
| ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS | Custom headers to add to requests ( Name: Value format, newline-separated for multiple headers). If a name or value contains a character an HTTP header can’t carry, such as a curly quote or a zero-width space, the request fails with an error that identifies the pair by position. Requires Claude Code v2.1.227 or later. Invalid request header value lists the exact character set and where the check runs. A value that sets a credential, org or tenant, routing, or API-behavior header, such as Authorization or Host , counts as a setting that needs approval when server-managed settings deliver it. From project or local settings, such a value follows the rules for when env values apply |

heading: ​ Variables
text:

| API_FORCE_IDLE_TIMEOUT | Override the 5-minute body idle timeout that aborts a streaming model response when no bytes arrive. Set to 0 to turn the timeout off, for example when a slow gateway or local model pauses longer than 5 minutes between chunks, or 1 to keep it on for every provider. When unset, the timeout is active on providers other than the direct Anthropic API, Claude Platform on AWS , and Amazon Bedrock with CLAUDE_ENABLE_BYTE_WATCHDOG_BEDROCK=1 set. The stream watchdogs run independently of it and abort a long silent pause even when you set 0 here |
| API_TIMEOUT_MS | Time in milliseconds that each API request attempt has to receive its response headers. It doesn’t limit how long a streaming response runs after that. The default is 600000, or 10 minutes, and the maximum is 2147483647. When you set a positive value, each attempt at a non-streaming request has to finish within it. Increase this when requests time out on slow networks or when routing through a proxy. Set to 0 to remove this limit, which requires Claude Code v2.1.305 or later. With 0 , a non-streaming attempt still times out after 300 seconds in a local session |
| AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK | Amazon Bedrock API key for authentication (see Amazon Bedrock API keys ) |

title: "Environment variables - Claude Code Docs"
heading: ​ Variables
text:
| BASH_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS | Default timeout for a foreground Bash or PowerShell tool command, in milliseconds (default: 120000, or 2 minutes). A value above the default time limit for background commands replaces that default in unattended sessions. The background time limit requires Claude Code v2.1.285 or later |
| BASH_MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH | Maximum number of characters of bash output that Claude Code reads back into a command’s result (default: 30000; maximum: 150000). If you set the bashOutputMaxChars setting, Claude Code ignores this variable. See Output limits |
| BASH_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS | Maximum timeout the model can set for a foreground Bash or PowerShell tool command, in milliseconds (default: 600000, or 10 minutes). The effective ceiling is the larger of this and BASH_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS . An effective ceiling longer than 2 hours also becomes the maximum time limit for background commands in unattended sessions. The background time limit requires Claude Code v2.1.285 or later |
| BETA_TRACING_ENDPOINT | OTLP/HTTP endpoint for detailed beta tracing : with ENABLE_BETA_TRACING_DETAILED=1 , logs and traces go there instead of to the configured exporters. Set it in your shell, user settings, or managed settings. Ignored in project and local settings |
| CCR_FORCE_BUNDLE | Set to 1 to force claude --cloud to bundle and upload your local repository instead of cloning from its remote |
| CLAUDECODE | Set to 1 in subprocesses Claude Code spawns (Bash and PowerShell tools, tmux sessions, hook commands, status line commands, stdio MCP server subprocesses). IDE extensions also set this in their integrated terminals. Use to detect when a script is running inside a subprocess spawned by Claude Code. To check whether the current process was spawned directly by a tool call or hook, rather than inside a stdio MCP server that Claude Code started, use CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION instead |

title: "Environment variables - Claude Code Docs"
heading: ​ Variables
text:
| CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_DISABLE_BUILTIN_AGENTS | Set to 1 to disable all built-in subagent types such as Explore and Plan. Only applies in non-interactive mode (the -p flag). Useful for SDK users who want a blank slate. This also removes general-purpose , the subagent Claude Code runs when an Agent tool call omits subagent_type . Such a call then fails with subagent_type is required |
| CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_MCP_NO_PREFIX | Set to 1 to skip the mcp__<server>__ prefix on tool names from SDK-created MCP servers. Tools use their original names. SDK usage only |
| CLAUDE_ASYNC_AGENT_STALL_TIMEOUT_MS | Stall timeout in milliseconds for subagents. Also covers workflow agents on Claude Code v2.1.286 or later. Default 600000 (10 minutes); if you raise CLAUDE_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS while the stream watchdog is on, the default rises with it, as Handle slow or stalled API responses describes |
| CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE | Set the percentage (1-100) of the auto-compact window at which auto-compaction triggers. Use lower values like 50 to compact earlier; the variable can’t raise the threshold, so values above the default percentage are ignored. It applies only in sessions that compact before the model’s context limit . Applies to both main conversations and subagents |
| CLAUDE_AUTO_BACKGROUND_TASKS | Set to 1 to force-enable automatic backgrounding of long-running agent tasks. When enabled, a subagent moves to the background after running for approximately two minutes. If Claude queued a tool call such as a file edit behind the subagent, the subagent finishes in the foreground before that call starts. Also enables automatic backgrounding of long MCP tool calls in non-interactive mode on Claude Code v2.1.212 or later |
| CLAUDE_AX_PREPARK_MS | In screen reader mode , how many milliseconds Claude Code waits before it writes a new or changed line. Default 0 , so Claude Code doesn’t wait. Before v2.1.287, the default was 50 . Claude Code caps the wait at 5000 . Requires Claude Code v2.1.233 or later |

title: "Environment variables - Claude Code Docs"
heading: ​ Variables
text:
| CLAUDE_AX_SCREEN_READER | Set to 1 to render screen-reader friendly output: flat text without decorative borders or animations. Set to 0 to force screen-reader mode off even when axScreenReader is true . The --ax-screen-reader flag takes precedence. Requires Claude Code v2.1.181 or later |
| CLAUDE_AX_STARTUP_QUIET_MS | In screen reader mode , how many milliseconds Claude Code holds the first interface render after the startup confirmation line, so your screen reader can speak the line in full before new output interrupts it. Default 3000 . Set 0 to render immediately. Claude Code caps the hold at 600000 (10 minutes). Your first keystroke ends the hold early. Requires Claude Code v2.1.217 or later |
| CLAUDE_BASH_MAINTAIN_PROJECT_WORKING_DIR | Return to the original working directory after each Bash or PowerShell command in the main session |
| CLAUDE_BYTE_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS | Timeout in milliseconds for the byte-level streaming idle watchdog; when set, it takes precedence over CLAUDE_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS for that watchdog and leaves the event-level watchdog unchanged. Claude Code clamps this variable to between 10 seconds and 30 minutes. Requires Claude Code v2.1.210 or later |
| CLAUDE_CLIENT_PRESENCE_FILE | Path to a file that an external tool, such as a screen-lock listener, creates when you unlock your screen and deletes when you lock it. While the file exists, Claude Code skips Remote Control mobile push notifications , so you stop getting pushes while you are actively using the computer. When the file is absent or unreadable, notifications are sent as normal. Claude Code checks the file once per push-triggering event rather than polling it. Requires Claude Code v2.1.181 or later |
| CLAUDE_CODE_ACCESSIBILITY | Set to 1 to keep the native terminal cursor visible and disable the inverted-text cursor indicator. Allows screen magnifiers like macOS Zoom to track cursor position |

title: "Environment variables - Claude Code Docs"
heading: ​ Variables
text:
| CLAUDE_CODE_ADDITIONAL_DIRECTORIES_CLAUDE_MD | Set to 1 to load memory files from directories specified with --add-dir . Loads CLAUDE.md , .claude/CLAUDE.md , .claude/rules/*.md , and CLAUDE.local.md . By default, additional directories do not load memory files |
| CLAUDE_CODE_ALT_SCREEN_FULL_REPAINT | Set to 1 to repaint the entire screen on every frame in fullscreen rendering instead of sending incremental updates. Use this if fullscreen mode shows stale or misplaced text fragments. Claude Code enables this automatically for background sessions and agent view on Windows |
| CLAUDE_CODE_ALWAYS_ENABLE_EFFORT | Set to 1 to send the effort parameter with every request, even when Claude Code does not recognize the model ID as effort-capable. Use this when routing through an LLM gateway or third-party provider that serves models under custom identifiers. Models that reject the effort parameter at the API, including Claude Opus 4.1, Claude Sonnet 4.5, Claude Haiku 4.5, and earlier models, are still excluded so requests do not fail |
| CLAUDE_CODE_API_KEY_HELPER_TTL_MS | Interval in milliseconds at which credentials should be refreshed (when using apiKeyHelper ) |
| CLAUDE_CODE_ARTIFACT_AUTO_OPEN | Set to 0 to stop Claude Code from opening the browser automatically when a new artifact is published |
| CLAUDE_CODE_ARTIFACT_COMMENTS | Set to 0 to stop Claude reading and replying to comments on an artifact . Has no effect when CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC has turned artifacts off . Requires Claude Code v2.1.221 or later |
| CLAUDE_CODE_ARTIFACT_COMMENTS_AUTOREACT | Set to 0 to stop Claude replying on its own to comments sent to it . Requires Claude Code v2.1.228 or later |
| CLAUDE_CODE_ARTIFACT_PUBLISH_EDITS | Set to 0 to stop Claude from applying small changes to an artifact’s file as part of publishing it. Claude then edits the file with its file-editing tools and publishes it as a separate step. Requires Claude Code v2.1.300 or later |

title: "Environment variables - Claude Code Docs"
heading: ​ Variables
text:
| CLAUDE_CODE_ATTRIBUTION_HEADER | Set to 0 to omit the attribution block , which carries the client version and a prompt fingerprint, from the start of the system prompt. Caching on a direct connection to the Anthropic API is unaffected either way. In some direct-connection setups, Claude Code keeps the block on auto mode classifier requests even when you set 0 . In System prompt attribution block , check which connections and credentials this covers. Before v2.1.181 the block included a per-request token on custom base URLs and Microsoft Foundry connections, so on those versions set it to 0 when your LLM gateway caches on the request body or forwards requests to a third-party provider, or when you connect to Microsoft Foundry directly |
| CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_BACKGROUND_WORKER_CHECKIN_SECONDS | Removed in v2.1.283. Use CLAUDE_CODE_WORKER_CHECKIN_SCHEDULE instead |
| CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW | Set the auto-compact window, how full the context gets before compaction, from 100000 to 1000000 tokens. Suffixed values such as 200k require v2.1.304 or later. For precedence over the other ways to set the window and the effect on the status line’s used_percentage , see Set the auto-compact window |
| CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_CONNECT_IDE | Override automatic IDE connection . By default, Claude Code connects automatically when launched inside a supported IDE’s integrated terminal. Set to false to prevent this. Set to true to force a connection attempt when auto-detection fails, such as when tmux obscures the parent terminal. Takes precedence over the autoConnectIde global config setting |
| CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_MODE_MODEL | Sets the model for the classifier requests Claude Code sends in auto mode . Use a full model ID such as claude-sonnet-4-6 . For the cases where Claude Code ignores it, see Choose the classifier model . Requires Claude Code v2.1.302 or later |

title: "Environment variables - Claude Code Docs"
heading: ​ Variables
text:
| CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_MODE_SERVER | Controls whether Claude Code asks the server to review auto mode actions . Set to 0 to use Claude Code’s own classifier requests instead. On a direct connection to the Anthropic API, requires v2.1.281 or later. The linked section lists which sessions ask the server when the variable is unset, and from which version. Requires Claude Code v2.1.271 or later |
| CLAUDE_CODE_AWS_CHAIN_RESOLVE_TIMEOUT_MS | Time in milliseconds Claude Code waits for the AWS default credential provider chain to produce credentials before the request fails with AWS default-chain credential resolve timed out (default: 60000 ). Raise it when a step in your chain legitimately needs longer, such as a browser-based SSO sign-in with MFA through a wrapper like aws-vault . Applies on Amazon Bedrock, Claude Platform on AWS , and the Mantle endpoint . See credential caching and resolution timeout . Requires Claude Code v2.1.207 or later |
| CLAUDE_CODE_BASH_EDIT_DIFF | Set to 0 to turn off the diff of the files that changed while a Bash command ran , or 1 to record it in every permission mode. Takes precedence over the bashEditDiffEnabled setting. Requires Claude Code v2.1.269 or later |
| CLAUDE_CODE_BG_TASKS_REPORT_RUNNING | Set to 0 to make a non-interactive session report an idle status to its host at every turn end, even while background work is still running. By default, the session keeps reporting a running status past turn end while background work such as a background agent or a workflow run is still live. This keeps a host that watches the status, such as a remote session list, from announcing that Claude is waiting for your input mid-work.
